title: Data tools: tables, sorting, validation, conditional formatting

questions.question: J1 has =SUM(tblSales[Amount]) and J2 has =SUM(G2:G21). You add a new invoice as row 22 of the Table. What happens?

answerOptions.text: J1 includes the new invoice; J2 does not
answerOptions.rationale: Table references grow with the Table, but a fixed range stays at G2:G21.

answerOptions.text: Both totals include the new invoice
answerOptions.rationale: G2:G21 is a fixed range, so row 22 is left out.

answerOptions.text: Neither total changes until you press ⌘ + T again
answerOptions.rationale: Tables expand on their own; ⌘ + T is only for creating one.
Structured references do not break when rows are added.

questions.question: You sort a Month column holding Apr, May, Jun and so on, and get Apr, Aug, Jul, Jun. Why?

answerOptions.text: You selected only the Month column
answerOptions.rationale: That would scramble rows, but the order would still be alphabetical.

answerOptions.text: Sort Ascending works only on numbers
answerOptions.rationale: Sort Ascending works on text as well.
Excel treats Apr, Aug and so on as plain text, so it sorts them A to Z.

answerOptions.text: The list is not an Excel Table
answerOptions.rationale: Ranges and Tables sort text the same way.

questions.question: In an Advanced Filter criteria range, row 2 has North under Region and >50000 under Amount, and row 3 has South under Region. Which rows are copied?

answerOptions.rationale: The second row adds South orders as an alternative.

answerOptions.text: North orders above 50,000, plus every South order
answerOptions.rationale: Conditions on the same row are AND; separate rows are OR.

answerOptions.text: North or South orders, all above 50,000
answerOptions.rationale: The >50000 condition is only on the North row.

answerOptions.text: All rows, because I3 is empty
answerOptions.rationale: A blank cell in a filled row just means no condition on that column for that row.

questions.question: Which formula, filled down from row 2, marks only the second and later copies of a mobile number in column D as Repeat?

answerOptions.rationale: This counts the whole column, so the first copy is also marked Repeat.
Both ends move together, so each row checks only itself.
A single cell can never count more than one.
Locking only the start makes the range grow, so it counts copies so far.

questions.question: A cell has a dropdown created with Data Validation. Someone copies a cell from another sheet and pastes it over it with ⌘ + V. What happens?

answerOptions.text: The paste replaces the validation rule along with the value
answerOptions.rationale: Validation checks typing, not normal pasting, so the rule is overwritten.

answerOptions.text: Excel blocks the paste with the error alert
answerOptions.rationale: Error alerts appear for typed entries, not for a normal paste.

answerOptions.text: The value is pasted and the dropdown stays
answerOptions.rationale: A normal paste brings the source cell's settings, removing the rule.

answerOptions.text: Excel asks whether to keep the rule
answerOptions.rationale: There is no such prompt.

questions.question: The formula in G2 is =SORT(UNIQUE(tblCities[State])). What should the dropdown Source be so the list grows when a new state is added?

answerOptions.rationale: That points at one cell only, so the dropdown shows one state.
The # refers to the whole spill range, whatever its length.
A fixed range will miss states added later.
This is not a valid reference.

questions.question: You select A2:F16 and add a formula rule to colour paid rows green. Which formula colours the whole row when column F says Paid?

answerOptions.rationale: Without the $, cell B2 checks G2, C2 checks H2, and so on.
Locking the row too makes every row check F2 only.
The $ locks the column, so every cell in the row checks column F.
This locks the row but lets the column shift across.

questions.question: Go To Special > Blanks has selected the empty cells in A2:A16, and you type =A2. Which key puts the formula into every selected blank at once on a Mac?

answerOptions.rationale: Plain Return enters the formula in the active cell only.
⌘ + D is Fill Down; it does not enter the formula you are typing into every blank.
⌘ + T toggles $ signs while you edit a formula.
⌃ + Return fills the entry into all selected cells.
